content: Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) is the seventh leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally. The standard treatment for EOC involves a combination of surgical debulking and platinum-based chemotherapy. However, between 55% and 75% of women who initially respond to first-line therapy experience disease relapse within two years. Second-line chemotherapy is primarily palliative, aiming to alleviate symptoms and extend survival. Advances in understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying EOC have led to the development of targeted therapies, including epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) and anti-EGFR antibodies. The objective of this review was to evaluate the efficacy and adverse effects of EGFR-targeted therapies in the treatment of EOC. The analysis included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing anti-EGFR agents, either alone or in combination with conventional chemotherapy, against conventional chemotherapy alone or no treatment in women with histologically confirmed EOC. From a total of 6105 references identified through database searches and an additional 15 references from grey literature, seven RCTs involving 1725 participants met the inclusion criteria. The findings are as follows: 1. Maintenance Treatment with Erlotinib (EGFR TKI) After First-Line Chemotherapy: Erlotinib likely has little or no effect on overall survival (hazard ratio [HR] 0.99, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.81 to 1.20; one study; 835 participants; low-certainty evidence). It may also have little or no effect on progression-free survival (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.23; one study; 835 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Quality of life data were incomplete, but the treatment may reduce quality of life compared to observation. 2. EGFR TKI (Vandetanib) for Relapsed EOC: Vandetanib may have little or no effect on overall survival (HR 1.25, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.95; one study; 129 participants; low-certainty evidence). It may also have little or no effect on progression-free survival (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.69 to 1.42; one study; 129 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Treatment with vandetanib may slightly increase the risk of severe toxicities, such as severe rash (risk ratio [RR] 13.63, 95% CI 0.78 to 236.87; one study; 125 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Quality of life data were not available for meta-analysis. 3. Anti-EGFR Antibody Treatment for Relapsed EOC: Anti-EGFR antibody therapy may or may not affect overall survival (HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.74 to 1.18; four studies; 658 participants; moderate-certainty evidence). It may or may not influence progression-free survival (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.70 to 1.16; four studies; 658 participants; low-certainty evidence). Anti-EGFR antibody therapy may or may not increase the risk of severe side effects, including: Severe nausea and/or vomiting (RR 1.27, 95% CI 0.56 to 2.89; three studies; 503 participants; low-certainty evidence). Severe fatigue (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.66 to 1.73; four studies; 652 participants; low-certainty evidence). Hypokalaemia (RR 2.01, 95% CI 0.80 to 5.06; three studies; 522 participants; low-certainty evidence). Severe diarrhea rates varied across studies (RR 2.87, 95% CI 0.59 to 13.89; four studies; 652 participants; low-certainty evidence). Subgroup analysis indicated that pertuzumab was associated with a higher risk of severe diarrhea (RR 6.37, 95% CI 1.89 to 21.45; three studies; 432 participants; low-certainty evidence) compared to seribantumab (RR 0.38, 95% CI 0.07 to 2.23; one study; 220 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Quality of life data were incompletely reported and could not be pooled for meta-analysis. In conclusion, current evidence suggests that anti-EGFR therapies, whether EGFR TKIs or anti-EGFR antibodies, provide little or no benefit in terms of survival outcomes, either as maintenance therapy following first-line chemotherapy or in combination with chemotherapy for recurrent disease. These treatments may increase the risk of certain adverse effects and may or may not negatively impact quality of life.
